speaker: J. J. Kohn
title: The d-bar Neumann problem and the Levi problem
summary: Kohn discusses solving \(\bar\partial u=\alpha\), the Levi form, and the passage from a local supporting holomorphic polynomial to a global nonextendible holomorphic function. The second page introduces the Dolbeault complex, the Neumann quadratic form, a boundary estimate, and the Kohn--Rossi extension paper. These are accounts of work already available before this talk, not announcements inferred solely from later publication dates \citep{kohn1963potential,kohn1963harmonic,kohn1964harmonic,kohnrossi1965extension}. The dated heading begins on P000090; P000088--P000089 belong to the preceding invariant-subspace discussion. A short reading programme at the end names algebraic groups and algebraic geometry.

speaker: R. Finn
title: Total curvature of complete open surfaces
summary: The brief entry recalls Gauss--Bonnet and Cohn--Vossen, illustrates the difference between closed and complete surfaces, and states the aim of replacing an inequality by an equality. Its final sentence is at the top of P000092, before Gelfand's new heading. Finn's 1965 article is a plausible publication context, but the surviving entry contains no end-defect formula with which to establish an exact theorem match \citep{cohnvossen1935curvature,finn1965conformal}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Atiyah-Bott: differential operators and elliptic complexes
summary: Gelfand begins an exposition attributed to Atiyah, introducing symbols, elliptic complexes, and the de Rham and Dolbeault examples. The speaker is Gelfand, not Atiyah. The reference underlying the sequence is the Harvard lecture material dated autumn 1964, preceding these meetings; its Russian translation appeared in 1966, and the journal article followed in 1967 \citep{atiyahbott1964notes,atiyahbott1967lefschetz}. The initial list of applications includes Brouwer, Lefschetz, eigenvectors, and Weyl characters. The symbol and finiteness discussions continue the topics indexed as 1964-28.2, 1964-28.4, and 1964-28.5; the underqualified earlier finiteness assertion 1964-28.3 should not be treated as a stronger theorem.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Atiyah-Bott: Lefschetz numbers, local terms, and Hodge theory
summary: The exposition resumes below the dated continuation heading on P000093. Gelfand defines endomorphisms of complexes and their Lefschetz numbers, describes a map with bundle lifts and simple fixed points, states the elliptic fixed-point formula, and starts its spectral proof. The main formulas require a consistent pullback convention, compactness, and the distinction between nonnegative spectrum and strictly positive eigenspaces \citep{atiyahbott1964notes}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Seminar programme for 1965-66
summary: The seven agenda entries propose Agranovich on integro-differential operators; Kirillov, Gelfand, or Dynin on Atiyah--Singer and the Cartan--Schwartz and Vishik seminars; Minlos on statistical physics; Graev on adeles; Kirillov and Gelfand on algebraic groups; Gelfand on Bott--Chern and zero distribution of sections; and Kazhdan on Riemann--Roch--Grothendieck. These are assignments and reading topics, not theorem statements. The Bott--Chern reference can be identified as the 1965 Acta Mathematica paper \citep{bottchern1965hermitian}. Kazhdan's talk begins separately in the lower part of the same page.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Algebraic varieties, rational equivalence, and the approach to Riemann-Roch
summary: The announced Riemann--Roch discussion starts with the foundations of classical algebraic geometry: affine sets, regular functions, ringed spaces, gluing, products, and separation. It then introduces cycles and their equivalence via \(\mathbb P^1\), ending with an unfinished proposed map \(K(X)\to A(X)\). The framework belongs to the earlier theory of coherent sheaves and Grothendieck's Riemann--Roch theorem \citep{serre1955coherent,borelserre1958riemannroch}. The last lines do not state a Riemann--Roch formula or a complete axiom system for Chern classes.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Elliptic complexes and the Hodge decomposition
summary: Gelfand repeats the symbol and geometric-endomorphism setup, chooses a density and metrics, and introduces the formal adjoint and Laplacian. The eigenspace cohomology assertion reaches the top of P000102. Dynin and Bernstein then intervene before the heading indicating that Gelfand resumes; these three headings are kept as separate catalogue records \citep{atiyahbott1964notes}.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Intervention on positive-eigenvalue cohomology
summary: The short intervention insists that nonzero eigenspaces give zero cohomology. The written justification then identifies cohomology with the kernel of a shifted Laplacian and asks about reapplying Hodge theory. That equation is not a valid proof: the shifted operator is not the nonnegative Hodge Laplacian of the original complex. Bernstein's immediately following intervention gives the direct contracting-homotopy argument.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Intervention giving the contracting homotopy
summary: Bernstein's named intervention follows Dynin and precedes the words indicating Gelfand's return. It derives the vanishing of positive-eigenvalue cohomology directly from \(\lambda s=dd^*s\). Catalogue record 62 is therefore placed before record 61 in actual source order.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Harmonic compression, trace regularization, and pseudodifferential operators
summary: The heading indicating Gelfand's return comes after both interventions. He compresses the chain map to Laplacian eigenspaces, obtains alternating trace cancellation, introduces the weighted trace series, and begins an oscillatory definition of pseudodifferential operators. That definition continues into the top of P000104, above the next dated heading. The argument follows the 1964 Harvard notes, especially their spectral and pseudodifferential sections \citep{atiyahbott1964notes,kohnnirenberg1965algebra}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Regularized traces and the local fixed-point trace
summary: The next dated continuation begins below the end of the pseudodifferential definition on P000104. Gelfand revisits index, finite-dimensional trace cancellation, and the spectral series; he then states the entire continuation theorem for a transverse geometric map and its equality at zero with the distributional flat trace. The final computation initially calls the delta integral the number of fixed points, omitting its Jacobian weight. The weights are restored explicitly in record 65 \citep{atiyahbott1964notes}.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Finite-type and coherent sheaves
summary: The five-minute intervention begins at the bottom of P000105 and continues into P000106. Kazhdan defines finite generation and coherence through relation sheaves, warns that one chosen presentation is not enough over a general ring, and states the closure and local-generation properties. Serre's coherent-sheaf paper is explicitly named \citep{serre1955coherent}.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: The algebraic definition of K-theory
summary: S. Gelfand introduces the Grothendieck group of projective modules, the splitting of its exact-sequence relations, localization over local rings, and the connection with vector bundles. He also asks what changes if all finite-type modules are used over a ring denoted \(E(X)\), whose exact identity is not explained. This heading precedes the new date 1 November and the Smirnov entry; it is therefore earlier in source order than catalogue record 65.

speaker: S. V. Smirnov
title: Extreme positive-definite functions on nilpotent groups
summary: The three-line entry asks for extreme points among positive-definite functions on groups obtained from nilpotent algebras by the Campbell--Hausdorff formula. It does not state the field, topology, normalization, or centrality condition. Smirnov's 1966 paper is a strong contemporaneous lead, received on 3 December 1965, but it treats normalized central positive-definite functions over a discrete field of characteristic zero. That restriction prevents an exact identification of the unrestricted notebook question \citep{smirnov1966positive}. The earlier normalized-central-function topic 1964-13.1 is thematically related; the missing centrality here prevents identifying the two questions.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The fixed-point trace and its real and complex applications
summary: After Smirnov's entry, Gelfand returns to Atiyah. He computes the delta-kernel trace with a Jacobian denominator, repeats the finite-complex trace lemma, and applies the formula to de Rham theory, complex structures, and projective transformations. The real de Rham calculation is identifiable; the complex-case notation and factors are too compressed to recover a unique asserted formula. The local inverse-map and ordinary-map conventions also conflict \citep{atiyahbott1964notes}.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Injectives and right derived functors
summary: Kazhdan defines injective objects and enough injectives, then constructs right derived functors of a left exact covariant functor through their long exact sequence, vanishing on injectives, and naturality. The final square and existence statement occupy the top of P000108 before Matsaev's new dated heading. This resumes the homological-algebra material already indexed as 1964-49.8; it is not a new open problem \citep{grothendieck1957homological}.

speaker: V. I. Matsaev
title: The Atiyah--Bott fixed-point formula
summary: The record begins at the dated Matsaev heading on P000108, after the preceding discussion of derived functors, and ends before Kazhdan on P000109. It gives the cohomological Lefschetz number of a geometric endomorphism of an elliptic complex, complex-power regularization, and the transverse-distribution interpretation of the local fixed-point contributions. The independent near-contemporary match is Bott's November 1965 Bourbaki exposition, which itself cites the 1964 Harvard notes. \citep{bott1966report}

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Coherent algebraic sheaves on affine varieties
summary: The Kazhdan heading lies on the lower part of P000109; his proof continues through the beginning of P000111. Principal affine opens, coherence of the structure sheaf, localization of sections, and affine acyclicity are presented in the tradition of Serre's \emph{Faisceaux alg\'ebriques coh\'erents}. An incomplete affineness-converse line is preserved as incomplete. \citep{serre1955coherent}

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Value distribution and Chern forms after Bott and Chern
summary: The dated heading on P000111 explicitly names Bott--Chern, \emph{Acta Mathematica} 114 (1965). Gelfand moves from Picard and Nevanlinna theory to spectral boundary conditions and an explicitly doubtful Banach-space extension, then introduces bundle-valued differential forms, connections, curvature and Chern forms. The record ends immediately before the Arnold heading on P000113. \citep{bottchern1965hermitian}

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Singularities and stability of differentiable mappings
summary: Arnold's heading begins below Gelfand's frame calculation on P000113; the final comment on a continuous smooth invariant extends onto the first lines of P000116. The record distinguishes Morse, fold and cusp singularities, discusses rank strata and Boardman symbols, and reports then-current claims of Thom and Mather. Arnold's 1968 lectures contain especially close matches, but their later publication is not evidence that the older Whitney and Morse results originated in this seminar. \citep{arnold1968singularities,boardman1967singularities,mather1971nice}

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Chern forms, Bianchi identity and curvature jets
summary: After the residual Arnold sentence at the top of P000116, the dated Gelfand heading restarts the connection and Chern-form construction. The new mathematical content is the Bianchi/transgression argument and a precise question about relations among curvature and its covariant derivatives. The latter is compared with the metric-jet isomorphism theorem, not classified as an untouched problem. \citep{bottchern1965hermitian,jentsch2026jet}

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Stability, preparation and intersections of invariant tori
summary: P000117 opens with Arnold on structural stability of flows and parameters, continues with planar desingularization and the Weierstrass--Malgrange division and preparation theorem, and P000118 introduces exact canonical transformations of \(T^n\times B^n\). The torus intersection claim is recognized as an early Arnold problem, with the notebook's graph argument recovered. Its \(2^n\) bound requires transversality; the exact-period condition also must be separated from an assumed Hamiltonian isotopy. \citep{malgrange1966ideals,chaperon1983questions,gong2023cuplength}

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Hermitian connections, cohomology from rings, and analytic canonical forms
summary: The dated Gelfand heading begins P000119. The discussion derives the Chern connection and its curvature, then reports Watts's October 1965 algebraic model for Alexander--Spanier cohomology. The Levinson and Whitney discussion on the upper part of P000121 has no intervening speaker heading and is assigned to this record by source sequence; Arnold's new heading begins the fluid discussion below it. The repeated Chern-form argument contains a genuine graded-sign error, and the Whitney example has five factors although the prose twice counts four surfaces. \citep{bottchern1965hermitian,watts1965alexander,lladser2007uniqueness,arnold1968singularities}

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: The topology of analytic stationary fluid flows
summary: Arnold's underlined heading on the lower part of P000121 begins this record, which ends immediately before the 13 December heading on P000122. It presents the commuting velocity and vorticity fields and the decomposition of an analytic steady flow by regular Bernoulli levels. Arnold's 1966 full paper gives an exact expanded match, explicitly referring to his earlier 1965 announcement. The notebook's separate compact-orbit lemma is too broad and is disproved here; individual dense streamlines must also be distinguished from the compact joint two-dimensional orbit. \citep{arnold1966geometrie}

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Ideal fluids and the geometry of invariant metrics
summary: The dated Arnold heading on P000122 starts this record. Newton's law and the incompressibility constraint lead to the Euler/Navier--Stokes equations; the discussion then sketches viscosity-dependent stability and gives the Lie-group interpretation of rigid-body and fluid motion. P000123 ends with the inertia operator, the bilinear adjoint \(B\), and a tangent/cotangent translation diagram. The actual Euler--Arnold evolution formula begins on the next page and belongs to the following record, not this one. Yudovich's named two-dimensional result is identified with his 1963 original paper. \citep{yudovich1963nonstationary,arnold1966geometrie}

title: The year 1966
summary: The boxed heading \ru{1966 г.} marks the resumption of the notebook. It contains no mathematical assertion. The attached catalogue gives a wider overlapping page range; the heading itself is on \GSpage{P000124}.

speaker: A. G. Kushnirenko
title: On invariant dynamical systems: title only
summary: Only Kushnirenko\textquotesingle s name, date and the title \ru{Об инвариантных динамических систем} survive. No definition of the invariant, theorem or proof follows before Gelfand\textquotesingle s heading. This is not sufficient evidence for identifying the talk with Kushnirenko\textquotesingle s entropy estimates from the preceding year (1964-10.2--3). Accordingly it has no invented mathematical item.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Ore fractions, Weyl fields, automorphisms and dimension
summary: The page begins with the Ore property and division rings of fractions, then distinguishes differential-operator rings \(R_{n,k}\) and their quotient division rings \(D_{n,k}\), introduces multiplicative leading symbols, and asks about determinants and all automorphisms. It ends with the growth definition of dimension and \(\dim R_{n,k}=2n+k\). The dimension formula in the handwriting lacks a logarithm in the numerator. Much of the page matches \citet{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; the paper was received on 19 January 1966, before this talk, but published afterwards. The general Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture for enveloping division rings is in that paper, not stated on this notebook page, and is not imported as a seminar item.

speaker: M. S. Agranovich
title: Pseudodifferential and singular integral operators
summary: The first Agranovich lecture introduces homogeneous symbols, spherical harmonic kernels, rough-symbol boundedness and the first rules of symbolic calculus. It is primarily an exposition of the already published 1965 theory, not a preview whose first publication was necessarily after the seminar. Several handwritten slips in the boundedness argument are separated from transcription mistakes. The lecture ends in the upper part of P000128, before Gelfand's integral-geometry heading.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Integral geometry on affine k-planes
summary: The lecture develops differential forms attached to the affine \(k\)-plane transform: a generalized determinant, a closedness criterion for the range, and inversion by integrating over cycles. The close publication is \citet{gelfand1967planes}, with Graev and Shapiro. Its hypotheses and quantifiers correct two potentially serious overstatements in the notebook. P000128 starts this record after Agranovich; P000132 ends it before Karpelevich.

speaker: F. I. Karpelevich
title: Klein on the spinning top
summary: A short exposition of Klein's Princeton lectures describes rotations by fractional linear transformations and reduces a top problem to an elliptic integral. The lecture crosses the page boundary: its final quadrature is at the top of P000133, before the dated Agranovich continuation. The two cyclic-momentum formulas contain a factor-of-two slip already present in the handwriting.

speaker: M. S. Agranovich
title: Symbolic calculus, elliptic operators and index
summary: The continuation assembles the local calculus on a manifold and derives the Fredholm and regularity theorems from a parametrix. It then states Seeley's special degree formula for the index and ends with Hörmander's oscillatory characterization. The exact Seeley theorem, including its equivalence with vanishing of lower-rank indices, was checked in the full paper's Russian translation; the 1965 English original is the historical publication.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Borel and Tits: algebraic and reductive groups
summary: This is an introductory report on Borel and Tits, not an announcement of a new classification. It passes from schemes and Chevalley's structure theorem to radicals, tori and root systems. Connectedness and the ground field are repeatedly tacit. The example calling an algebraic torus an abelian variety is incompatible with the standard algebraic-group meaning of torus and is retained as a source-level error.

speaker: V. A. Borovikov; comment by I. M. Gelfand
title: Boundary integrals and area
summary: After the dated March heading, Borovikov states a double boundary cosine integral for area. Gelfand follows with a very compressed slice-area/volume formula. The former is valid with convexity and consistent inward chord-angle conventions; it has no missing distance denominator. The latter is false for a single slicing direction and remains uncertain as a historical assertion because an angular average may have been omitted.

speaker: V. B. Lidskii
title: Zeta function of all zeros of an exponential-type entire function
summary: This compact announcement has an unusually exact later match: Lidskii and Sadovnichii's 1967 paper, especially Lemmas 2--3. The entire continuation concerns a branch-dependent sum over all nonzero zeros, with complete sectorial asymptotics. The comparison with the ordinary zeta function refers to the difference between all signed sine zeros and only the positive half.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Generalized parabolic equations and cone-valued ellipticity
summary: Gindikin's announcement precedes Minlos in the physical notebook, although the catalogue numbers it 89. The 1967 multidimensional-time paper identifies both the hyperbolic replacement of the time derivative and the \(V\)-elliptic mapping. A reinspection corrects the transcription's pseudo-operator to hyperbolic operator. The random-walk/heat sentence before the boxed Minlos heading is recorded here with attribution uncertainty.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Ising lattice gas and thermodynamic limit
summary: The boxed Minlos heading introduces a lattice-gas configuration sum and the limit of its logarithm per volume. This is a brief substantive reminder, not a content-free heading, but no low-temperature contour theorem or phase-transition statement is actually recorded. It recurs to the elementary material indexed as 1964-3.1 and 1964-3.2.
